This covers all the changes cleanly. Here's my summary.

## Summary

Migrated the `sec-insights` backend's chat LLM transport from direct OpenAI Chat Completions to Router's OpenAI Responses-compatible `/v1/responses` surface.

**Core changes:**
- `app/llama_index_settings.py`, `app/chat/engine.py`: replaced `llama_index.llms.openai.OpenAI` (Chat Completions) with `llama_index.llms.openai.OpenAIResponses`, pointed at `RAMP_ROUTER_BASE_URL`/`RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY`.
- `app/chat/engine.py`, `app/chat/tools.py`: replaced `llama_index.agent.openai.OpenAIAgent` with `llama_index.core.agent.FunctionCallingAgent`. `OpenAIAgent` hard-requires `isinstance(llm, OpenAI)` (the Chat Completions class), which rejects `OpenAIResponses`; `FunctionCallingAgent` only requires `FunctionCallingLLM`, so it works with either.
- Bumped `openai`, `llama-index-core`, `llama-index-llms-openai` (→0.4.7, which adds `OpenAIResponses`), `llama-index-agent-openai`, `llama-index-question-gen-openai` in `pyproject.toml` — all within already-compatible version ranges, verified by installing and running the full test suite.
- `app/core/config.py`: added `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY`, `RAMP_ROUTER_BASE_URL` (default `https://api.router.com/v1`), `ROUTER_CHAT_MODEL` (replaces hardcoded `OPENAI_CHAT_LLM_NAME`). Model IDs are account-specific per Router's `/v1/models`, so I didn't invent a default — `ROUTER_CHAT_MODEL` must be set via env var from your account's model list.
- Set `strict=True` on both `OpenAIResponses` instances: the Responses API defaults function tools to `strict=true` server-side, and llama-index only emits the required `additionalProperties: false` when told to — without this, every tool call was rejected (confirmed against the simulator).
- `tools.py`: changed `Settings.llm.model_copy(..., deep=True)` to `deep=False` — `OpenAIResponses` eagerly builds its httpx client in `__init__`, which can't be deep-copied.
- Updated `.env.development`, `Dockerfile`, `render.yaml`, `README.md` to plumb the new Router env vars alongside the existing ones.

**Kept unchanged:** `OpenAIEmbedding` still calls OpenAI directly with `OPENAI_API_KEY` — Router has no embeddings endpoint, so this is explicitly out of scope per the task's own instructions. All prompts, tool definitions, and retry policy are untouched.

**Verified:**
- Full baseline test suite (import/compile checks + pytest) passes unchanged.
- Against the local Router simulator: a plain text-only request round-tripped correctly, and a tool-calling request (the polygon.io agent) also validated successfully after the `strict=True` fix — confirmed via `router-sim received N request(s), N valid`.
- Updated `poetry.lock` isn't regenerated (no `poetry` binary available in this sandbox) — run `poetry lock` before deploying.

**Could not fully resolve:** `FunctionCallingAgent` is deprecated in this llama-index-core version in favor of `llama_index.core.agent.workflow.FunctionAgent`, scheduled for removal in core 0.13.0. It works correctly now and was the minimal-risk choice compatible with the rest of this app's pinned 0.12.x stack, but it's worth a follow-up migration before upgrading core past 0.12.x.
